title: AI Support Replies: Keep a Human in Control
rights: Original APEX/RMC AI Workshop educational writing and typography-only visuals. CMU Flite slt synthetic narration rendered locally with FFmpeg; no third-party media, brand marks, real customer data, or music.
description: A free practical checklist for owners testing AI-assisted customer support: classify the request, redact sensitive information, draft for a human, and test uncertain cases. Fictional examples only. No AI reply is automatically sent, no live helpdesk service is claimed, and no sales lift is promised. Optional opt-in small-business response workflow inquiry: https://apex-content-worker-production.up.railway.app/home-services. Public checkout remains paused.

scenes.heading: Drafting is not sending
scenes.text: Keep one human decision before any reply leaves.
scenes.narration: An AI tool can help draft a customer reply, but a draft is not permission to send. Start with human review and a clear path for exceptions.

scenes.heading: 1. Classify the request
scenes.text: Routine question | missing facts | urgent human review
scenes.narration: A fictional cleaning business receives three messages: a request for hours, a disputed invoice, and a safety complaint. These need different handling. Do not treat all three as routine.

scenes.heading: 2. Hide private details
scenes.text: Use a sample ID. Mask contact and payment fields.
scenes.narration: Before trying a new workflow, replace real names, phone numbers and payment details with fictional values. Keep only the fields needed to decide who should review the request.

scenes.heading: 3. Draft with uncertainty
scenes.text: Unknown price or policy? Ask the owner, not the model.
scenes.narration: If the booking price, refund rule or appointment availability is unknown, the draft should say that a team member needs to confirm. Never invent a refund or promise a booking.

scenes.heading: 4. Route high-risk cases
scenes.text: Safety, billing disputes and complaints need a person.
scenes.narration: Set a simple rule for urgent safety issues and billing disputes. Flag the request for an authorized human. Do not allow an automatic response to close the case or make a financial commitment.

scenes.heading: 5. Test before enabling
scenes.text: Try duplicates, blanks, wrong categories and restarts.
scenes.narration: Use fictional messages to test duplicate submissions, missing details, uncertain classification and a worker restart. Confirm that every case stays reviewable and that no duplicate message is sent.

scenes.heading: 6. Measure the outcome
scenes.text: Track reviewed drafts, corrections and exceptions.
scenes.narration: Count how many drafts a reviewer accepts and corrects. Also count exceptions and the time spent reviewing. A synthetic demonstration cannot establish customer satisfaction or increased revenue.

scenes.heading: Free first step
scenes.text: Start with one human-reviewed response template.
scenes.narration: Write one response template and an escalation checklist before buying more automation. RMC AI Workshop shares educational examples. The APEX home services page accepts optional inquiries, without requiring a purchase.
